title: Barbarina rehearsal and the hostile hostess
summary: At the Barbarina Cabaret on Hardenbergstrasse the hostess Ellie Glasner insulted the band in German, objecting to a Black leader with white musicians.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And so we opened -- there was something very funny about the opening. I arrived with the orchestra naturally for an artist's rehearsal.
We were sitting on the stand, waiting
Briggs
for artists to appear.
This was in Berlin?
In Berlin.
At the Barbarina Caberet.
The Barbarina.
On Hardenbergstrasse.
Hardenbergstrasse?
Yes. Hardenbergstrasse in Berlin. And this cabaret was owned by Mr. and Mrs. Tischauer, T-i-s-c-h-a-u-e-r.
Right.
Tischauer. And after a while, a lady came in -- we didn't know who she was, but she came in and she looked over the orchestra and she started saying some insulting things in German.
Well, some of the boys, Chappy [Eugene Obendorfer] the drummer, who was of Hungarian origin, he understood it. He understood the German.
He said to me, "She's not satisfied." So I said, "Well, what about?" He said, "She's not satisfied." She said, in German, she said,
Briggs
"Das kammt nicht dier fager." "It's impossible." "It can't happen." One of those things. Referring to me.
Because you were the only black guy in the band, and you were the leader of the band?
That's correct, yes.
A black leader and white musicians?
Yes. And she didn't like that. The artists came, half of them brought books, had the orchestra take up parts, and we looked, went over everything together.
Then, I asked the artists. I said, "Okay, now if something goes wrong, as far as the tempo, let me know."
So, we started the rehearsal and the first act okay. The second act okay. The third act, okay. She didn't know any of us at all.
